items.title: Centuries of child labor left lasting spinal damage in Dutch children, study finds
items.summary: Children in the postmedieval Dutch workforce worked so hard that their spines became worn and deformed, with some children affected before they even had a chance to lose their baby teeth, a new study published in the International Journal of Paleopathology finds.

items.title: Keto diet cut liver fat by 67% in a clinical trial
items.summary: A ketogenic diet outperformed Mediterranean and low-fat diets in several measures of metabolic health during a clinical trial involving people with obesity, prediabetes, and fatty liver disease. items.title: Dogs may hold surprising clues to human longevity
items.summary: Dogs and humans may have more in common when it comes to aging than scientists realized. Researchers with the Dog Aging Project found that patterns of small molecules in dogs’ blood were linked to longer or shorter lifespans in remarkably similar ways to those seen in people. items.title: Dva velika oceana stoljećima su bila usklađena. Sada se taj odnos raspada
items.summary: NOVA studija pokazuje da globalno zatopljenje narušava stoljetnu vezu između Pacifika i Indijskog oceana. Ta promjena, jača od utjecaja vulkana, otežava klimatska predviđanja za Afriku i Aziju.

items.title: Scientists turn one of the hardest plastics to recycle into high-performance engine lubricant
items.summary: Researchers have discovered a way to turn notoriously difficult-to-recycle PVC plastic into a key ingredient used in high-performance lubricants such as engine oil. The technique could give mountains of plastic waste a valuable second life while making lubricant production more sustainable.

items.title: Talking to your children about consent and sexual violence can be hard. Here's how to start the conversation
items.summary: There have been multiple high-profile alleged incidents of sexual violence against women and girls in news headlines this month. Some involve teenage boys.

items.title: Nano-sandwich photocathode improves solar conversion of CO₂ into ethanol
items.summary: Czech researchers at Charles University in Prague, led by Pavla Eliášová, have developed an advanced photocathode that helps convert the greenhouse gas carbon dioxide into pure ethanol using sunlight. items.title: The universe is still speeding up, but nobody knows why
items.summary: A major new analysis challenges recent claims that the universe's expansion is slowing, finding that the evidence for cosmic acceleration remains strong. items.title: Long-term melatonin use linked to 90% higher heart failure risk
items.summary: People with chronic insomnia who used melatonin long term had a roughly 90% higher risk of developing heart failure over five years, according to a large preliminary study. items.title: Australia’s red soil may be hiding a massive clean energy source
items.summary: Researchers have discovered that Western Australia’s iron-rich rocks can naturally generate hydrogen and that the process may be boosted to produce much larger amounts. items.title: Your sleep may be hiding an early clue to Alzheimer’s
items.summary: Frequent micro-awakenings during sleep were linked to higher genetic risk for Alzheimer’s in healthy middle-aged adults who had no symptoms. The discovery raises the possibility that subtle changes during sleep could offer an early warning signal years before memory problems appear.

items.title: Scientists discover why damaged nerves struggle to heal
items.summary: Scientists have identified a protein that acts like a brake on the nervous system’s ability to repair damaged connections. items.title: Many cities buried urban streams. Here's how to bring them back
items.summary: As many cities developed, streams that once flowed on the surface were buried underground to make way for growing infrastructure. However, as heavier rainfall, extreme weather and aging infrastructure place growing pressure on cities, these buried streams could become part of the solution.

items.title: Rethinking bluegreen aphid control as insecticide resistance spreads
items.summary: When an insecticide application fails to control bluegreen aphid, application conditions may not be the only cause. Research has identified resistant populations across southern Australia, confirming that repeated reliance on broad-spectrum insecticides is no longer sustainable.

items.title: How AI‑powered policing is endangering the public's trust in police
items.summary: Since the release of ChatGPT in 2022, artificial intelligence (AI) has dominated the cultural landscape. Uptake across various sectors, including law enforcement, quickly followed, usually with minimal foresight and little to no guardrails, like effective policies or laws, to govern AI use.

items.title: Climate policy could learn from people who already live within the limits of sufficiency

items.title: The discovery of the Great Barrier Reef's whale maternity ward
items.summary: It started with a simple message: "This is the year to do something small for something huge." Now, 17 years later, the Whitsundays region has some of the best protection in the world for migrating humpback whales.

Trump on Aug. 28, 2026, for their service during the Artemis II mission.

items.summary: Temperatures have warmed dramatically across the equatorial Pacific Ocean in 2026, signaling the onset of a strong and potentially historic El Niño. items.title: Earlier swathing opens a new pathway for subterranean clover seed harvest
items.summary: Subterranean clover's ability to bury its seed supports pasture persistence but makes commercial seed harvesting difficult. The industry relies on aging Horwood-Bagshaw (HB) suction harvesters, which collect seed from fully dry crops after repeated tillage and raking.

items.summary: NASA named a team from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) as the first prize winner for Phase 2 of the agency’s LunaRecycle Challenge, which focused on developing solutions for reducing waste durin

items.title: Diverse portfolio of protected areas key to Mexican conservation efforts
items.summary: In 2020, Mexico joined 150 nations committing to protect 30% of its territory by 2030 as part of the global 30x30 initiative. More than halfway through the decade, there is ongoing debate about how to effectively expand protected areas to meet that ambitious goal.

items.title: Low temperature graphene growth opens a route to sustainable resource recycling
items.summary: Graphene is an exceptionally useful material for creating batteries, catalysts and electronic devices. items.title: Dog-friendly dining isn't just a trend, it's good for business, new research shows
items.summary: Restaurants that go beyond simply allowing dogs on patios by offering dedicated menu items for them can significantly boost customer traffic, spending and word-of-mouth, according to new research from Toronto Metropolitan University.

items.title: Fast fashion's carbon footprint can be reduced across its life cycle, new study suggests
items.summary: Fast fashion is built on cheap, short-lived garments, especially cotton and polyester T-shirts. items.title: Scientists capture first molecular-level images of water reorganization during a reaction crucial for life
items.summary: Some of nature's most important chemical reactions rely on the coupled movement of negatively and positively charged particles. These processes play central roles in photosynthesis, catalysis and biological energy conversion yet remain difficult to observe.

items.title: Does the Nepal glacier collapse signal a new climate risk?
items.summary: Does the devastating flooding unleashed by the collapse of a section of a glacier in the Nepali Himalayas signal a new kind of risk in a world warmed by climate change? Here's what scientists told AFP.

items.title: Honey bees can serve as sentinels for environmental health
items.summary: Honey bees (Apis mellifera) are widely known as essential pollinators, but researchers using a "One Health" approach have also identified them as biological sentinels of environmental health. items.title: SpaceX recovers Starship from the Indian Ocean a month after launch and is shipping it back to Texas
items.summary: SpaceX has pulled off its biggest salvage operation yet, recovering its most recently launched Starship from the Indian Ocean.

items.summary: To strengthen the nation’s space workforce and develop the next generation of space leaders, President Donald J. items.title: Motorboat noise stunts growth and impairs predator escape in reef fish, study shows
items.summary: Coral reef fish that are exposed to motorboat noise grow up smaller and less able to dodge predators, new research shows. Scientists played either boat noise or natural reef sounds to a species from the Great Barrier Reef called the spiny chromis, both as embryos and soon after hatching.

items.title: Why some earthquakes caused by fracking come with warning signs
items.summary: Fracking, the injection of high-pressure fluid to fracture rock and release oil or gas, can trigger earthquakes. While some sites generate small tremors beforehand that may provide an early warning, others produce few or none.

items.title: Joro spiders eat wider range of insects than Georgia's native orb weavers
items.summary: When Joro spiders first arrived stateside more than a decade ago, scientists worried the massive black-and-yellow spiders would gorge themselves on the same bugs as native spiders (or even the native spiders themselves). items.title: Less buying power, elevated inflation push down consumer views
items.summary: Consumer sentiment dropped about 6% from last month, landing around 11% below a year ago amid continued worries that inflation will remain elevated for the foreseeable future, according to the University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers.

items.title: Widespread use of AI tools could make it harder to craft effective business communications

items.summary: The evolutionary histories of Earth and Mercury differ fundamentally. items.title: Germany could miss climate goal in 2026 for the first time: Think tank
items.summary: Germany risks missing an annual climate target in 2026 for the first time unless cuts to greenhouse gas emissions sharply accelerate, a think tank warned Friday.

items.title: Indonesia escalates battle against fires, putrid haze
items.summary: Indonesia has intensified efforts to fight wildfires with cloud seeding and water bombing as thousands of people nationwide battle to breathe through smoke and haze, officials said Friday.

items.title: Once a legend, humpback whales make a comeback in Brazil
items.summary: Female humpback whales off the coast of Brazil now have their pick of mates, who slap the water with their tails and jostle for attention—a scene that would have been unthinkable a few decades ago.

items.summary: Thirty-five years on—well, 12 million, technically—Ashfall Fossil Beds State Historical Park continues to offer important glimpses of prehistoric life in Nebraska.

items.title: Why a newly formed lake is sparking fears of more flooding along the Nepal-China border
items.summary: Even as rescuers worked through mud and debris Friday in areas devastated by a catastrophic flash flood along the Himalayan border between Nepal and China, authorities warned that a newly formed, overflowing lake could trigger further flooding.
